samples.summary: Undo/redo selection restore strips the new `lineAffinity` from presence endpoints
samples.evidence: `restoreSelectionFromPresence`'s local `clampPos` rebuilds each endpoint as `{ blockId: pos.blockId, offset: Math.min(pos.offset, maxOffset) }` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1974-1978) and the rebuilt objects are what `selection.setRange(range)` receives at editor.ts:1995. The store now anchors and resolves endpoint affinity (yorkie-doc-store.ts:999-1004, 1077) and publishes it into `activeSelection` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:3005), and the branch's own plan states the change is so "peer selections and undo/redo restore keep it" (docs/tasks/active/20260822-selection-line-affinity-todo.md:49-52). This caller was not updated, so after undo/redo a highlight whose start sat on a wrap boundary falls back to the default reading and can re-open on the line above — the exact bug the change fixes elsewhere.

samples.summary: Undo/redo caret restore drops caret `lineAffinity`, and the store getter's return type makes it unreadable
samples.evidence: editor.ts:2018 (undo) and editor.ts:2044 (redo) do `cursor.moveTo({ blockId: restoredPos.blockId, offset: Math.min(...) })` — no affinity on the position and no affinity argument — while `restoreLocalCursor` in the same file (editor.ts:3592-3610) was changed precisely because dropping the affinity "would undo the anchor round-trip and re-collapse the caret onto the previous visual line". The affinity is not even reachable here: `getPresenceCursorPos()` is declared `{ blockId: string; offset: number } | undefined` and casts presence to that shape (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:2912-2927), so the published `lineAffinity` is type-erased for this consumer even though `DocsPresence.activeCursorPos` now declares it (packages/frontend/src/types/users.ts:24).

samples.summary: `cursor.position.lineAffinity` and `cursor.lineAffinity` are now two unsynchronised sources of truth; the presence publisher reads the position one
samples.evidence: `Cursor.moveTo(pos, affinity = 'backward')` stores the affinity twice: on `this.position` (whatever the caller put there) and on `this.lineAffinity` (the argument) — packages/docs/src/view/cursor.ts:28-32. Rendering uses `this.lineAffinity` (cursor.ts:48) but the presence broadcast uses `cursor.position` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1160 and 2069 → docs-view.tsx:399 `store.updateCursorPos(pos, sel)` → yorkie-doc-store.ts:2999), and `restoreLocalCursor` now re-applies `cursorPos.lineAffinity` (editor.ts:3592-3610). Call sites where the two disagree: text-editor.ts:1544 passes the mousedown `pos` (which now carries `lineAffinity`, text-editor.ts:1521-1525) with no affinity argument, so the caret renders 'backward' but publishes 'forward'; text-editor.ts:3381 and 3446 `this.cursor.moveTo(start)` reuse a normalized selection endpoint that may still carry a click affinity after the selected text was deleted. On the next remote change the caret is restored with an affinity it was never rendered at.

samples.summary: Keyboard-driven carets still lose their affinity on the presence round-trip, so the restoreLocalCursor fix is mouse-only
samples.evidence: The non-shift arrow path does `this.cursor.moveTo(newPos, isVertical ? this.cursor.lineAffinity : hAffinity)` (text-editor.ts:2795) and `handleHome` does `moveTo(newPos, 'forward')` (text-editor.ts:2818) — in both cases `newPos` is a bare `{blockId, offset}`, so `cursor.position` carries no `lineAffinity`. Since the publisher passes `cursor.position` (editor.ts:1160/2069), a caret placed at a wrap boundary by ArrowRight/Home publishes no affinity and `restoreLocalCursor` (editor.ts:3592) re-collapses it to the default 'backward' after any remote edit — the failure mode the diff's own comment says it is fixing. Same gap for anchors read from `cursor.position` (text-editor.ts:1620, 2774, 2807, 2826): the known `cursor.lineAffinity` is not attached.
searchedFor: read cursor.ts and editor.ts fireCursorMoveCallbacks sites

samples.summary: Peer caret still hardcodes 'backward' while peer selection now honours the published affinity
samples.evidence: Peer selections go through `computeSelectionRects(peer.selection, ...)` (editor.ts:1620) which now reads each endpoint's `lineAffinity`, but the peer caret is resolved with a literal `'backward'` at editor.ts:1561-1568 even though `peer.position` may now carry `lineAffinity` (packages/frontend/src/types/users.ts:24, forwarded verbatim by docs-view.tsx:226). At a wrap boundary a peer's caret and the edge of their highlight will render on different visual lines. The users.ts comment acknowledges this, but the inconsistency lives in the docs package consumer.

samples.summary: Default start affinity flipped backward→forward for every non-selection consumer of computeSelectionRects
samples.evidence: `startAffinity = start.lineAffinity ?? 'forward'` (selection.ts:259) now flows into `positionToPagePixel`/`findPageForPosition` for the paragraph branch, which previously always used the 'backward' default (`findPageForPosition`'s default, pagination.ts:385). Consumers that never set an affinity therefore change rendering when a range starts exactly on a wrap boundary: search-match highlights (editor.ts:1640) and the search scroll-to-match that reads `rects[0].y` (editor.ts:3129-3137), comment marker rects used for hit-testing (editor.ts:1659-1668, built from tree paths in packages/frontend/src/app/docs/comments/decorations.ts:24-27), spell-error underlines (editor.ts:1676) and the text-box editor's own selection (packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:560, which has no lineAffinity anywhere). Probably an improvement, but it is an unflagged behaviour change to out-of-diff consumers with no coverage.

verdict.reason: All four cited locations exist exactly as described. editor.ts:2018 (undo) and editor.ts:2044 (redo) restore the caret with `cursor.moveTo({ blockId, offset: Math.min(...) })` — no lineAffinity field and no affinity argument — whereas restoreLocalCursor at editor.ts:3592-3608 in the same file deliberately carries the affinity both ways, with a comment stating that dropping it re-collapses the caret onto the previous visual line at a wrap boundary. The reader is also type-erased: yorkie-doc-store.ts:2912-2930 declares/casts getPresenceCursorPos() to `{ blockId; offset } | undefined`, and editor.ts:2012/2038 re-declare that same narrowed shape in the local cast, so lineAffinity is unreadable at the undo/redo consumer even though DocsPresence.activeCursorPos declares it (types/users.ts:21-28) and updateCursorPos actually publishes it (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2972-3007). This is a widened contract with an unupdated consumer in another package, on the reachable editor undo/redo handlers; no guard makes it unreachable and it falls in the blast-radius lane, so I have no named ground to refute.

finding.summary: Resolved caret `lineAffinity` is dropped by the only production consumer: `restoreLocalCursor` rebuilds the position without the field and calls `cursor.moveTo(pos)` with no affinity argument

verdict.reason: The finding's core claim — that `restoreLocalCursor` "rebuilds the position without the field and calls `cursor.moveTo(pos)` with no affinity argument" — is factually wrong for this working tree. `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:3592-3611` both spreads `lineAffinity` into the rebuilt position and passes `cursorPos.lineAffinity` as the second (affinity) argument to `cursor.moveTo`, with a comment explaining exactly why. `Cursor.moveTo` (packages/docs/src/view/cursor.ts:28-32) therefore assigns the resolved affinity; its `'backward'` default only applies when the resolved position carries no affinity at all, which matches the documented caret default in packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:200-214. So the claimed divergence between the local render and the `publishResolvedLocalCursor` broadcast (docs-view.tsx:375-378) cannot occur, and the proposed fix ("pass cursorPos.lineAffinity through to moveTo") is already implemented. Grep confirmed there is only one implementation of `restoreLocalCursor` (editor.ts:3592), one interface declaration (editor.ts:130), and one production caller (docs-view.tsx:368) — no shadowing variant that drops the field. Ground: not-present.

finding.summary: Undo/redo selection restore strips endpoint `lineAffinity`, which the new start-defaults-to-'forward' rule turns from harmless into a rendering change
finding.evidence: `restoreSelectionFromPresence`'s local `clampPos` returns `{ blockId, offset }` only (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1974-1978), discarding the `lineAffinity` that `getPresenceSelection()` now returns on each endpoint (published by yorkie-doc-store.ts:3005 via `anchorDocRange`/`clampPosToModel`, and typed in packages/frontend/src/types/users.ts:33-34). Previously dropping it was inert because every consumer defaulted to `'backward'`; this PR's documented default (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:200-206, implemented at packages/docs/src/view/selection.ts:260) makes an affinity-less START read `'forward'`. So an undo-restored selection whose start was recorded with an explicit `'backward'` affinity at a wrap boundary now paints beginning on the following visual line instead of where the user selected. Fix on `clampPos`: spread the endpoint's `lineAffinity` through.

verdict.reason: The finding checks out end to end. `clampPos` in `restoreSelectionFromPresence` returns only `{blockId, offset}` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1974-1978) and is applied to both restored endpoints (editor.ts:1989-1990), so endpoint `lineAffinity` is discarded before `selection.setRange` (editor.ts:1995). The affinity it discards is genuinely present on the restored value: selection endpoints receive explicit affinity in text-editor.ts:2778 (shift+arrow focus, which becomes the range START for a backwards selection) and text-editor.ts:2813; `Selection.setRange` keeps endpoints verbatim (selection.ts:686-692) and normalization preserves each endpoint's affinity into `start` (selection.ts:703-713); `setCursorForHistory` synchronously flushes that selection into presence as Yorkie's undo reverse (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2878-2884, called from editor.ts:1951-1954) and `clampPosToModel` explicitly spreads `lineAffinity` through (yorkie-doc-store.ts:969-973, 2991-3007), with `getPresenceSelection()` returning a `DocsSelection` typed to carry it (packages/frontend/src/types/users.ts:33-34). And the new default really changes the reading of an absent start affinity from the historical 'backward' to 'forward' (documented at packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:200-208, implemented at packages/docs/src/view/selection.ts:260-261), so a stripped, explicitly-'backward' start now paints the highlight beginning on the following visual line at a wrap boundary. The sibling `restoreLocalCursor` path deliberately carries affinity through for exactly this reason (editor.ts:3592-3608), confirming the omission is an unupdated consumer rather than an intentional choice. This is in the blast-radius lane (changed default/contract with an unupdated consumer outside the diff), reachable by shift-select -> edit -> undo, and no downstream guard re-attaches affinity. No ground for not-present, already-guarded, or out-of-scope.
